pages.title: How to use this checklist
pages.lead: Use it before you pay for a resell-rights product, and again before you list anything from one. It is a decision aid, not a verdict, and it does not read or interpret your licence for you.

steps.title: Find the licence text
steps.text: Get the actual licence (PDF or page) you will receive. Sales-page claims, captions and DMs are not the licence.

steps.title: Name the rights type
steps.text: Note the exact words the licence uses: PLR, MRR, Resell Rights, Personal Use. Sellers use them inconsistently (page 3).

steps.title: Check the platform
steps.text: Read the rules of the place you plan to sell. Platform rules apply on top of any licence (page 5).

steps.title: Check what’s inside
steps.text: Canva elements, AI output, stock, music, fonts and logos may carry their own terms (page 6).

steps.title: Decide and record
steps.text: Use the scenarios, red flags and worksheets, and save check dates. For high stakes, get qualified professional advice.

callout.label: READ THIS FIRST
callout.text: This guide is educational. It does not grant any resale, PLR or MRR rights. It is not legal advice, and it is for your personal use only. Rules change: check the current official pages before you rely on them.

legend.label: GREEN-LEANING
legend.text: Official text supports it in the usual case — only under the stated conditions.

legend.label: AMBER
legend.text: Depends on specific conditions, or the official text is silent. Confirm the named point first.

legend.label: RED
legend.text: Official text prohibits it, or the risk is high. Don’t go ahead as described.

legend.label: VERIFY BEFORE RELYING
legend.text: Not checked against official text this round. Check the official source yourself.

pages.title: Five terms sellers use loosely
pages.lead: PLR, MRR and Resell Rights are not the same thing. These are common trade usages, not official definitions. The licence text you receive decides — not the label on the sales page.

cards.label: PLR · PRIVATE LABEL RIGHTS
cards.text: Usually means you may edit the content and put your own name on it. What you may then do — sell it, give it away, pass rights on — varies by licence. Permission to edit or add your name is not the same as owning the copyright: check what the licence actually grants. Gumroad names PLR resale specifically (page 5).

cards.label: MRR · MASTER RESELL RIGHTS
cards.text: Usually means you may resell the product and also pass resale rights on to your buyers. Some MRR licences say the product may not be edited, even when the marketing says “rebrand it as your own”. If the sales page and the licence differ, ask the seller in writing before you pay.

cards.label: RR · RESELL RIGHTS
cards.text: Usually means you may resell the product as it is, to end users, without passing resale rights on. Price limits, bundling, giveaways and where you may sell are often not stated. If the licence doesn’t say, ask before you assume.

cards.label: PERSONAL USE
cards.text: You may use it yourself. No selling, giving away or sharing copies. If a licence does not clearly say what you may do, don’t assume you have more than personal use.

callout.label: AFFILIATE — A DIFFERENT THING
callout.text: You promote someone else’s product with a tracked link and earn a commission; the creator makes the sale. You don’t get a copy to sell. Different rules apply (page 7).

pages.title: Before you buy: seven questions
pages.lead: Answer these before you pay. Any “no” or “don’t know” is your answer for now.

steps.title: Is there a written licence?
steps.text: Can you read the full licence before paying? If not, treat it as RED until you have it in writing.

steps.title: What does it actually grant?
steps.text: Which words appear — PLR, MRR, Resell Rights, Personal Use? May you sell, edit, rebrand, give away, pass rights on?

steps.title: Where do the rights come from?
steps.text: Does the licence say who created the product and who granted the rights? If you can’t trace it, treat it as AMBER.

steps.title: Where will you sell?
steps.text: Gumroad, Beacons, Etsy or your own site? Check that platform’s rules (page 5). A seller’s licence does not change them.

steps.title: What’s inside the files?
steps.text: Canva elements, AI output, stock photos, music, fonts, brand logos? Each may have its own terms (page 6).

steps.title: How is it marketed to you?
steps.text: Income screenshots, “100% profit”, “buy to unlock your affiliate link”? Read pages 7–8 before paying.

steps.title: Can you get your money back?
steps.text: Read the refund terms before paying. Save the licence, the sales page and the date.

callout.label: HOW TO READ THE EXITS
callout.text: No licence (A) or a platform that bans it (D) = RED. Anything unclear in B, C or E = AMBER until answered in writing. Clear on every step = GREEN-LEANING for that platform, on those terms only.

pages.title: Platform rules, word for word
pages.lead: Quoted from saved copies of each official page. Platform rules sit on top of any licence: a seller’s licence does not change them.

cards.label: GUMROAD · PROHIBITED PRODUCTS AND ACTIVITIES
cards.title: PLR resale is named. MRR and RR are not.
cards.text: The list includes “reselling private label rights products”. It also lists “services (including, but not limited to, ‘get rich quick’ schemes, business opportunities, investment opportunities…)” and “multi-level marketing or pyramid schemes”. MRR and plain resell rights are not named in the PLR line. Don’t assume either way: read the other lines and ask Gumroad.
cards.note: “If you are unsure whether your content is prohibited on Gumroad, please contact us” · the list “may change abruptly and without notice”

cards.label: BEACONS · COMMUNITY STANDARDS (STORE)
cards.title: Resale is generally not allowed
cards.signal_label: RED · PRODUCTS YOU DID NOT CREATE
cards.text: “In general, we do not allow resale; you cannot sell products you did not create. You can act as an affiliate for other creators on Beacons, but you cannot sell products that aren’t your own creation.” Also prohibited: “Multi-level marketing offers, work-at-home scams and make money online opportunities”.
cards.note: Also listed as high-risk: “Unlicensed proprietary content” and “Multi-level Marketing or Pyramid Schemes”

cards.label: ETSY · CREATIVITY STANDARDS
cards.title: Digital downloads must be the seller’s own designs
cards.text: Items “designed by a seller” “include only” listed types, among them “Digital downloads of sellers’ original designs: Original content created by the seller, sold as a digital download.” Listed as not qualifying: “A bundle, collection, scan, or PDF of someone else’s work” and “A PDF file of a book that the seller did not personally create or design”.
cards.note: “Etsy reserves the right to remove listings that do not follow our policies.”

callout.label: SELLING FROM YOUR OWN WEBSITE
callout.text: These marketplace lists don’t apply there, but the licence and the terms of content inside the pack still do. Your payment provider may have its own rules — VERIFY; not checked in this guide.

pages.title: Third-party content inside the pack
pages.lead: A resell licence comes from the pack seller. Items inside may be under someone else’s terms — check each one.

cards.label: CANVA LIBRARY CONTENT · CLA §9
cards.text: Canva’s Content License Agreement §9 says you “definitely can’t” “sub-license, re-sell, rent, lend, assign, gift or otherwise transfer or distribute the Content or the rights granted under this Content License Agreement (subject to section 4A)”, or use Content “in a manner that gives the impression that the Content was created by you”.
cards.note: BEFORE BUYING — Ask which Canva items are inside and whether they come as Canva links or as files.

cards.label: AI-GENERATED CONTENT · PROVIDER TERMS
cards.text: OpenAI (US Terms of Use): “As between you and OpenAI, and to the extent permitted by applicable law, you (a) retain your ownership rights in Input and (b) own the Output.” That wording is between OpenAI and its user and doesn’t mention later buyers; “output may not be unique”. Anthropic: “Subject to your compliance with our Terms, we assign to you all of our right, title, and interest—if any—in Outputs.”
cards.source: OpenAI Terms of Use (US) · Anthropic Consumer Terms §4
cards.note: BEFORE BUYING — Ask which AI tools made it. For copyright in AI output, see Can I Use This?

cards.label: STOCK PHOTOS · VIDEO · MUSIC · FONTS
cards.text: Each comes under a licence from wherever it was obtained. A pack’s “resell rights” can’t tell you what those licences allow, and “no watermark” is not a licence. Canva’s font software may only be used on Canva or inside an exported Canva design (CLA §9A).
cards.note: BEFORE BUYING — Ask for a source list. No list? You can’t check it.

cards.label: BRAND LOGOS IN “LUXURY” CLIPS
cards.text: “Luxury lifestyle” packs often show car badges, watch faces and fashion logos. A pack licence cannot give you those brands’ permission. Beacons: “We do not allow the uploading of any content that infringes on copyrights, trademarks, or patents.”
cards.note: BEFORE BUYING — Ask to see sample clips. Visible logos are a red flag (page 16).

pages.title: Promoting is not reselling
pages.lead: Promoting a product with an affiliate link is not the same as reselling it. Both can be restricted, for different reasons.

cards.label: RESELLING
cards.text: You list and sell a copy yourself, from your own shop, under a licence from the pack seller. The platform’s resale rules apply to your listing (page 5).

cards.label: PROMOTING AS AN AFFILIATE
cards.text: You share a tracked link; the creator makes the sale and delivers the product. Beacons: “You can act as an affiliate for other creators on Beacons, but you cannot sell products that aren’t your own creation.” An affiliate link is not a licence to copy or resell the product.

cards.label: WHAT’S BEING PROMOTED MATTERS
cards.text: Beacons prohibits “Multi-level marketing offers, work-at-home scams and make money online opportunities”. Gumroad prohibits “services (including, but not limited to, ‘get rich quick’ schemes, business opportunities, investment opportunities…)” and “multi-level marketing or pyramid schemes”. If a course is mainly about earning by promoting that same course, read these lines first.

cards.label: QUESTIONS TO ASK BEFORE YOU JOIN
cards.text: How many commission levels are there — only your own sales, or also sales by people you sign up? Does most of the income described come from promoting this same course, rather than from using what it teaches? Must you buy before you can promote? What are the refund terms?

callout.label: WHAT THIS PAGE DOES NOT DO
callout.text: These questions help you decide what to check. They are not a test of whether any programme is legal, multi-level marketing or a pyramid scheme — that is a question for a qualified professional.

pages.title: Income screenshots, testimonials and disclosure
pages.lead: Three US FTC topics matter here but have not yet been checked against official FTC pages, so they are marked VERIFY. This guide makes no income claims.

cards.label: US FTC · ENDORSEMENT DISCLOSURE
cards.text: The US Federal Trade Commission has guidance on endorsements, including disclosing a paid or commission relationship such as an affiliate link. This edition has not checked the official FTC text, so no wording, section or date is given here.
cards.note: VERIFY BEFORE RELYING — official FTC page not yet checked

cards.label: US FTC · FAKE OR MISLEADING TESTIMONIALS
cards.text: The FTC also has rules on fake or misleading reviews and testimonials. Reusing a seller’s testimonials, or presenting other people’s results as your customers’, may be relevant. Not yet checked against the official FTC text.
cards.note: VERIFY BEFORE RELYING — official FTC page not yet checked

cards.label: US FTC · EARNINGS CLAIMS
cards.text: An FTC Earnings Claim Rule has been proposed. This edition has not checked its current status, or any other FTC rule on earnings claims, against official FTC text. Check the current FTC position before you make any income statement.
cards.note: VERIFY BEFORE RELYING — official FTC page not yet checked

cards.label: PLATFORM RULES · INCOME SCREENSHOTS
cards.title: Someone else’s results are not your results
cards.text: Gumroad’s list includes “deceptive marketing practices”. Beacons’ Email Marketing guidelines, under Prohibited Actions, bar including in your “Campaigns, Websites, Ads, or account or sell in your Store any material that wasn’t created by you, provided for you to use, or that would violate anyone’s rights”. Note the “provided for you to use” wording: check what the seller gave you in writing.
cards.source: Gumroad (Sep 16, 2026) · Beacons, Email Marketing · Prohibited Actions (Nov 22, 2025)
cards.note: BEFORE POSTING — Show no income figure you can’t prove from your own records.

pages.title: Real-world resell scenarios
pages.lead: First-pass signals, not permission. Check the licence you actually received.

items.title: Rebrand a PLR ebook and sell it on Gumroad
items.why: Gumroad’s list includes “reselling private label rights products”. A new cover and title don’t tell you it has stopped being a PLR product.
checks: Licence allows editing, rebranding and selling?
How much is still the original PLR text?
Unsure? Ask support@gumroad.com before listing
Canva, AI or stock content inside (page 6)?
Licence and check date saved (page 18)
items.change: Gumroad changing its list, or confirming your version in writing. A product you wrote yourself is a different case (scenario 5).

items.title: List an MRR course on Beacons
items.why: Beacons: “In general, we do not allow resale; you cannot sell products you did not create.” A course you bought is not one you created.
checks: Did you create any of it yourself?
Is it pitched as a way to make money online?
Other people’s videos, music or clips inside?
Is the creator on Beacons with an affiliate option?
Rule and check date saved (page 19)
items.change: Beacons changing its Store rules. Promoting the creator’s own listing as an affiliate is a different route (scenario 8).

pages.title: Real-world resell scenarios
pages.lead: First-pass signals, not permission. Check the licence you actually received.

items.title: Sell a PLR planner on Etsy
items.why: Etsy digital downloads must be “sellers’ original designs”; “A bundle, collection, scan, or PDF of someone else’s work” does not qualify.
checks: Is the design yours, or the PLR author’s?
Would your changes make it your own design?
Canva template or elements inside (page 6)?
AI used? Disclose it in the listing description
Does the licence allow resale at all?
items.change: Designing your own planner, using the PLR only as research, moves this toward scenario 5 — then check Etsy’s rules again.

items.title: Sell a PLR or MRR pack on your own website
items.why: No marketplace list applies, but the licence still sets what you may do, and items inside the pack keep their own terms.
checks: Licence allows selling from your own site?
Any price, bundle or territory limits?
Canva, AI, stock, music or fonts inside?
Payment provider rules — VERIFY, not checked here
Refund and delivery terms you’ll give buyers
items.change: GREEN-LEANING if the licence clearly allows it and every asset inside is cleared. RED if the licence is personal use only or missing.

pages.title: Real-world resell scenarios
pages.lead: First-pass signals, not permission. Check the licence you actually received.

items.title: Use a PLR pack to learn, then write your own
items.why: Reading it for your own learning is personal use. A product you then write yourself, from your own knowledge, is not a copy of the pack.
checks: Licence allows at least personal use?
Written from scratch, not paraphrased line by line?
No images, templates or files copied over
Your own examples, structure and title
Your platform’s rules still apply to your product
items.change: AMBER if your version follows the pack closely in structure or wording — that is scenario 6.

items.title: Heavily rewrite PLR text and sell it
items.why: PLR licences often allow editing, but none of the platform rules quoted here say how much rewriting makes a PLR product your own.
checks: Licence allows selling an edited version?
Any licence rule on names, credits or changes?
Gumroad: still a PLR product? Ask if unsure
Etsy: is it now your original design?
Keep drafts that show your own work
items.change: GREEN-LEANING if it becomes genuinely your own writing (scenario 5). RED where the platform treats it as PLR resale.

pages.title: Real-world resell scenarios
pages.lead: First-pass signals, not permission. Check the licence you actually received.

items.title: Give a PLR pack away as a lead magnet
items.why: Giving copies away still distributes them. Some licences allow giveaways; others don’t mention them — and silence is not permission.
checks: Licence mentions free giveaways?
Allowed in exchange for an email address?
Gumroad $0 listing: still “reselling”? Ask
Third-party content inside (page 6)?
Your name or brand on it — allowed?
items.change: GREEN-LEANING if the licence expressly allows free giveaways and the delivery platform allows it. RED if the licence is personal use only.

items.title: Promote the original course as an affiliate on Beacons
items.why: Beacons lets you “act as an affiliate for other creators on Beacons”, but prohibits “Multi-level marketing offers, work-at-home scams and make money online opportunities”.
checks: Creator on Beacons with an official affiliate link?
Is the course mainly about earning by promoting it?
How many commission levels are there?
Must you buy before you can promote?
Commission disclosed (FTC — VERIFY)
items.change: GREEN-LEANING for an ordinary product, clearly disclosed. RED if the offer falls in Beacons’ prohibited list.

pages.title: Real-world resell scenarios
pages.lead: First-pass signals, not permission. Check the licence you actually received.

items.title: Reuse the seller’s income screenshots
items.why: They show someone else’s results, not yours or what a buyer can expect. Gumroad lists “deceptive marketing practices”; FTC rules are relevant (VERIFY).
checks: Provided for you to use, in writing?
Would viewers think they’re your results?
Can you prove every figure you show?
Are typical results stated?
FTC earnings and testimonial rules — VERIFY
items.change: Use no income figures. If you must, show only your own verifiable records, after checking the FTC pages (VERIFY).

items.title: A Canva template pack with “full resell rights”
items.why: Canva’s licence is “non-transferable (subject to section 4A below)”, and CLA §9 bars you from “sub-license, re-sell … or otherwise transfer or distribute the Content”. A pack’s “full resell rights” can’t add to that.
checks: Canva library template, or seller’s own design?
Any Pro (crown) elements inside?
Delivered as a Canva link or as files?
Can elements be extracted as files?
See Can I Sell This? for Canva detail
items.change: AMBER if the pack holds only the seller’s own designs with no Canva library Content — then check Can I Sell This? first.

pages.title: Real-world resell scenarios
pages.lead: First-pass signals, not permission. Check the licence you actually received.

items.title: An AI-generated pack with resell rights
items.signal_label: AMBER · ASK WHO MADE IT, AND HOW
items.why: OpenAI’s ownership clause begins “As between you and OpenAI” — wording between OpenAI and whoever generated it, silent on later buyers — and says “output may not be unique”.
checks: Which AI tools and plans made it?
Did the seller check those providers’ terms?
Could others have near-identical output?
Real brands, people or characters in it?
Etsy: disclose AI; “AI prompt bundles” don’t qualify
items.change: GREEN-LEANING if the seller names the tools, their terms fit and the licence is clear. RED if it contains logos, characters or real likenesses.

items.title: A “luxury lifestyle” clip vault with brand logos
items.why: Car badges, watch faces and fashion logos are other companies’ trademarks, and each clip was filmed by someone. A pack licence can’t grant brand permission, or filmmaker rights the seller doesn’t hold.
checks: Who filmed each clip? Is there a source list?
Does each clip’s licence allow resale?
Visible logos, products or recognisable people?
Is the music in the clips licensed?
“No watermark” is not a licence
items.change: AMBER only if every clip has a documented licence allowing redistribution and no brand marks are visible.

pages.title: Real-world resell scenarios
pages.lead: First-pass signals, not permission. Check the licence you actually received.

items.title: Add resell products as a bonus
items.signal_label: AMBER · A BONUS IS STILL DISTRIBUTION
items.why: A “free bonus” still hands buyers a copy. The licence must allow bundling, and your platform may treat the bonus as part of what you sell.
checks: Licence allows bundling or bonuses?
Any minimum-price or “never free” rule?
Would the bonus be banned alone on this platform?
Contents inside cleared (page 6)?
Bonus “value” used as a sales claim?
items.change: GREEN-LEANING if the licence expressly allows bonuses and the item would be allowed on its own. RED on a platform that bans it.

items.title: Sell “master resell rights” so buyers can resell
items.why: You would pass rights on, so every gap in the chain reaches your buyers too. Beacons: “In general, we do not allow resale”; Gumroad doesn’t name MRR — check its PLR and business-opportunity lines.
checks: Licence lets you grant MRR to others?
Rights traceable back to the creator?
Which platform — does it allow this at all?
Marketed as an income opportunity?
Can you answer your buyers’ licence questions?
items.change: A written licence expressly allowing onward MRR, cleared contents and a platform that allows it could move this to AMBER. Never assume it.

pages.title: Red flags before you buy
pages.lead: Any one of these: stop, and get answers in writing before you pay or list.
items: No licence text before you pay — only a sales page, caption or DM.
The sales page says “rebrand it as your own” but the licence says no edits (or the reverse).
The seller can’t say who created the product or where their rights come from.
It is marketed with “100% profit” claims or income screenshots.
You must buy before you can promote or earn.
Most of the income described comes from selling the same course to the next buyer.
Commissions on sales made by people you sign up (more than one level).
“Luxury” clips with visible car, watch or fashion logos.
Music, stock footage or fonts with no named source or licence.
Canva templates sold with “full resell rights”.
“No watermark” offered as proof you can use it.
You’re told to sell on Gumroad, Beacons or Etsy with no mention of their rules.
No refund terms, or refunds only if you “take action” first.
Pressure: countdown timers, “last spots”, DM-only pricing.

callout.label: WHAT A RED FLAG MEANS
callout.text: A red flag doesn’t prove anything is illegal or that any seller acted wrongly. It means you don’t yet have enough to decide.

pages.title: Before-you-list checklist
pages.lead: Run this before every listing, including free ones.
items: I have the full licence text saved, with the date I received it.
The licence clearly allows what I plan to do: sell, edit, rebrand, give away or pass rights on.
The licence matches what the sales page promised — or I asked the seller in writing.
I can trace who created the product.
I checked my platform’s current rules and saved the page date (page 5).
Gumroad: I read the PLR and business-opportunity lines, and asked support if unsure.
Beacons: I created this myself — or I’m promoting as an affiliate, not reselling.
Etsy: the design is my own original work, and any AI use is disclosed in the listing.
I know every Canva, AI, stock, music and font asset inside, and its terms.
No brand logos, recognisable people or characters I don’t have rights to.
No income figures or screenshots I can’t prove from my own records.
Any affiliate relationship is clearly disclosed (FTC — VERIFY).
My listing tells buyers exactly what rights they get — and don’t get.
I filled in the worksheets (pages 18–19).

pages.title: Licence record
pages.lead: One record per product. Copy the licence’s own words; don’t summarise from memory.
fields: LICENCE TYPE AS WRITTEN (PLR / MRR / RR / PERSONAL USE / OTHER)
MAY I SELL IT? WHERE? ANY PRICE LIMITS?
MAY I EDIT, REBRAND OR PUT MY NAME ON IT?
MAY I GIVE IT AWAY OR BUNDLE IT?
MAY I PASS RESALE RIGHTS ON?
WHO CREATED IT / WHERE DO THE RIGHTS COME FROM?
THIRD-PARTY CONTENT INSIDE (CANVA, AI, STOCK, MUSIC, FONTS, LOGOS)
SALES-PAGE CLAIMS THAT DIFFER FROM THE LICENCE
QUESTIONS SENT TO SELLER + DATE + ANSWER

pages.title: Platform & rights check
pages.lead: One row per place you might sell or promote. Quote the rule; don’t paraphrase it.

pages.title: Safer paths, from clearest to riskiest
pages.lead: From clearer ground at the top to the most friction at the bottom.

levels.label: LOWER FRICTION
levels.text: Create an original product from your own knowledge, words and assets

levels.label: GREEN-LEANING
levels.text: Use PLR only to learn, then write your own with your own expertise and examples

levels.label: AMBER
levels.text: Recommend a product as a disclosed affiliate, where the platform allows it and the offer isn’t on its prohibited list

levels.label: HIGHER FRICTION
levels.text: Resell only with a clear written licence and cleared contents, on a platform that allows it

levels.label: AVOID
levels.text: Reselling with no written licence, on a platform that bans it, or with uncleared content inside

callout.label: START AT THE TOP
callout.text: Each step down adds rules to check and records to keep. None of these steps is a guarantee — check the current rules each time.
